findings.title: Searching for something unknow
findings.summary_md: Secure Annex researcher John Tuckner identified more than 50 hidden Chrome extensions that put nearly 6,000,000 users at risk of cookie theft. The extensions are unlisted in the Chrome Web Store and were promoted through ads and malicious sites, carrying broad permissions over browsing and cookies.

findings.title: Chrome extensions with 6 million installs have hidden tracking code
findings.summary_md: A set of 57 Chrome extensions with 6,000,000 users was discovered with risky capabilities including monitoring browsing behavior, accessing cookies for domains, and potentially executing remote scripts. The extensions are hidden from Chrome Web Store searches and can only be installed via direct URL, and many were promoted through ads and malicious sites. Researcher John Tuckner traced them through a shared domain, unknow.com, found in an obfuscated extension named Fire Shield Extension Protection.

findings.title: Over 50 malicious Chrome extensions are secretly spying on you
findings.summary_md: Secure Annex researcher John Tuckner identified 57 malicious Chrome extensions that can be used to track user activity or run malware, with over 6 million downloads. The most popular extension was Cuponomia with 700,000+ users, followed by Fire Shield Extension Protection and Total Safety for Chrome with 300,000+ users each. The extensions were promoted through ads and scam sites using false promises of increased security or real-world earnings.

findings.title: Report: 57 Unlisted Chrome Extensions Exposed 6 Million Users to Cookie Theft, Tracking Risks
findings.summary_md: Enterprise security firm Secure Annex identified a network of 57 unlisted browser extensions that potentially exposed nearly 6 million users to cookie theft and pervasive tracking. Working with Obsidian Security, Secure Annex compiled the list of suspect extensions, which request broad permissions including access to user cookies and authentication tokens. The extensions are not discoverable through standard Chrome Web Store searches and require a direct URL for installation.

findings.title: 57 suspicious Chrome extensions with millions of installs
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky covered 57 suspicious Chrome extensions with 6 million installs, traced by researcher John Tuckner to an obfuscated extension named Fire Shield Extension Protection found hidden in the Chrome Web Store. The extensions carry broad permissions such as monitoring browsing behavior, accessing cookies, and modifying search providers. Kaspersky noted that hidden extensions in official stores are sometimes used by threat actors to evade detection.
